full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.
proof: Basis proof of the complete selected target Scope and representations. Keep all original hypotheses: p is any prime; K is any field of characteristic p; λ is an integer with 0≤λ0 and I={0,...,λ}, formally Fin(n). Returning to the original integer parameter is the identity λ=(Int.toNat λ:ℤ). All occurrences of factorials, binomial coefficients and index subtraction below have natural arguments; λ−2i in a scalar weight denotes integer subtraction, not truncated natural subtraction. View the original free abelian subgroup M as its ℤ-submodule in V. Its inclusion ι:M→V is injective. An integer basis that is also a complex basis has exactly n elements: the latter basis has cardinal n by the given complex dimension. Reindex it by I. Thus the header predicate admissibleLattice is exactly an encoding of the original lattice condition: it asserts such paired bases and stability under all divided powers. Stability under their generated ℤ-algebra follows by sums, integer multiples and compositions, so is equivalent to the stated U_ℤ-stability. The header highestWeightData packages the commutator, vector and dimension consequences of the original assumptions; it does not assert or replace complex irreducibility. Complex irreducibility remains an original H, but the argument actually uses only those consequences. No nonzero condition on the operator h is introduced, which matters when λ=0. Endomorphism products mean composition, with the rightmost factor applied first. Prepared native basis facts. B001 is independence of eigenvectors for injectively indexed eigenvalues. B002 says a linearly independent family of the same finite cardinality as the dimension spans. B003 extends a ℤ-basis b of M to the K-basis 1⊗b of K⊗_ℤ M. B004 says r! maps to a unit in characteristic p when ri; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ, and 0 otherwise. For the first nonzero case the numerator accumulated by x^r is (λ−i+1)...(λ−i+r)=(λ−i+r)!/(λ−i)!; division by r! gives the displayed binomial by B005. For the second it is (i+1)...(i+r)=(i+r)!/i!, again giving the binomial by B005. All divisions in this paragraph occur only in ℂ, where the factorials are nonzero. In the remaining cases the iterate reaches x e_0=0 or y e_λ=0 before the required number of steps. This proves every clause of B101, including r=0. B102. Construct integer endomorphisms with cleared matrix-unit identities. Let E_ij be the complex-linear map e_j↦e_i, e_k↦0 for k≠j, and let c_j=binom(λ,j), a natural integer. Formula B005 shows c_j j!(λ−j)!=λ!, so c_j>0; it also gives binom(λ,λ−j)=c_j by swapping the factorial factors and cancelling their positive product. Set P=Y_λ X_λ. If k<λ, X_λ e_k=0. On e_λ, X_λ e_λ=e_0 and Y_λ e_0=e_λ. Thus P=E_λλ. The B101 formulas also give X_{λ−i}e_λ=e_i with coefficient 1. To compute P Y_{λ−j}, start with e_k. If kj, that Y operator is zero by termination. If k=j, the value before P is binom(λ,λ−j)e_λ=c_j e_λ. Consequently A_ij := X_{λ−i} P Y_{λ−j} = X_{λ−i} Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ−j} = c_j E_ij (a) as complex-linear endomorphisms. Admissibility ensures every factor of A_ij preserves M, so A_ij restricts to a ℤ-linear endomorphism of M. The E_ij themselves are NOT asserted to preserve M. In End_ℂ(V), evaluation on e_t gives E_ij E_kl=E_il if j=k, and 0 if j≠k; ∑_i E_ii=Id. Using (a), it follows that A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il if j=k, and 0 if j≠k. (b) Define the natural integers C=∏_{t∈I} c_t, d_i=∏_{t∈I,t≠i} c_t. The product with no factors is 1. Finite product decomposition gives C=c_i d_i for each i, and hence ∑_{i∈I} d_i A_ii = C Id. (c) Equations (b) and (c) use only integer scalars and endomorphisms preserving M. For any m∈M their two sides have the same image in V by the complex identities. The injectivity of ι then proves the equalities ON M. This equality argument uses no tensor-injectivity claim and no rational scalar action on M. Likewise r! X_r=x^r and r! Y_r=y^r, initially equalities in End_ℂ(V), restrict to equalities of ℤ-endomorphisms of M for every r. Since X_1=x, Y_1=y preserve M, the commutator xy−yx also preserves M, and its restriction is the h action. These statements prove B102. B103. Extend the integer identities to the original reduced module. First work on T=K⊗_ℤ M. It has a K-basis β_i=1⊗b_i by B003, for ANY of the paired lattice bases b fixed above. Thus by B006 dim_K T=n, and the finite spanning basis proves finite-dimensionality. T is nonzero: for example β_0≠0 by independence of a basis over the nontrivial field K. This proof does not use a reduction of the complex coordinate basis e_i. For every ℤ-endomorphism f of M, use B007 for its extension f̂. The basis elements 1⊗b_i span T, and indeed all pure tensors c⊗m span: write m=∑_i z_i b_i with z_i∈ℤ and expand by the balanced tensor relations. The formula f̂(c⊗m)=c⊗f(m) proves that scalar extension preserves addition, integer scalar multiplication (with the integer cast into K), composition and the identity. For composition, f̂ ĝ(c⊗m)=c⊗f(g(m)); for sums it is c⊗(f(m)+g(m)); for an integer z, c⊗(z f(m))=(zc)⊗f(m), the balanced relation. Equality on the displayed spanning tensors proves equality of the K-linear maps. Finite sums and powers follow by induction. Thus no assumed faithful scalar extension, flatness, or unspecified ring map on endomorphisms is needed. For r≤λ0, dim_F U=n, and F_ij (i,j∈Fin(n)) satisfy (d) and the multiplication relations in the B104 statement. Let W be a subspace invariant under them. If W=0 the desired alternative holds. Otherwise choose w∈W with w≠0. Equation (d), evaluated at w, gives ∑_j F_jj w=w. Hence at least one j has u=F_jj w≠0; if all terms were zero their sum would be zero. Invariance gives u∈W, and F_jj u=u by idempotence. Put u_i=F_ij u for all i∈Fin(n). Each u_i∈W. For a relation ∑_i a_i u_i=0 and fixed k∈Fin(n), apply F_jk. The product relation says F_jk u_i=F_jk F_ij u=0 if k≠i, F_jk u_k=F_jj u=u. Thus a_k u=0. As u≠0 and F is a field, a_k=0 (otherwise multiply by its inverse). All coefficients vanish, proving linear independence of the finite family u_i. Its cardinality is n=dim_F U, so B002 makes its span all of U. Since W contains every u_i it contains their span, and W=U. This proves the universal dichotomy in B104 without a hypothesis of algebraic closure. B105. Apply the derivations to the full selected target. Use the original complex representation and ANY admissible lattice. The Chevalley relations and highest-weight vector supply B101, hence B102; the original prime, field and bound λ
lean_header:
import Mathlib

namespace YuiObjects

noncomputable def dividedPower {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (a : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((Nat.factorial r : ℂ)⁻¹) • (a ^ r)

def stable {F V : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
    (a : Module.End F V) (W : Submodule F V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ W, a w ∈ W

def highestWeightData {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℕ) (h x y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) : Prop :=
  v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v ∧
  h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧
  h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧
  x * y - y * x = h ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = lam + 1

def admissibleLattice {V : Type*} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (lam : ℕ) (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  (∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℤ M)
      (e : Module.Basis (Fin (lam + 1)) ℂ V), ∀ i, (b i : V) = e i) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower x r (m : V) ∈ M) ∧
  (∀ (r : ℕ) (m : M), dividedPower y r (m : V) ∈ M)

def matrixUnits {F V I : Type*} [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] (f : I → I → Module.End F V) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j k l, f i j * f k l = if j = k then f i l else 0) ∧
  (∑ i, f i i) = 1

end YuiObjects

dependencies.statement: For every field F, F-vector space V, index type I, endomorphism f, injective function μ:I→F and family z:I→V of nonzero eigenvectors with eigenvalues μ(i), the family z is F-linearly independent.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib environment supplied for this task; declaration and source read with read_mathlib.

lean.type: ∀ (F V I : Type*) [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V] (f : Module.End F V) (μ : I → F) (z : I → V), Function.Injective μ → (∀ i, f.HasEigenvector (μ i) (z i)) → LinearIndependent F z
lean.proof:
intro F V I _ _ _ f μ z hμ hz
exact f.eigenvectors_linearIndependent' μ hμ z hz

dependencies.justification: Direct instance of the indexed eigenvector independence theorem. Applied only over ℂ in B101; no independence of characteristic-p weights is assumed.

dependencies.statement: For any field F, finite-dimensional F-vector space V, finite index type I, and linearly independent family z:I→V with |I|=dim_F(V), the F-linear span of the family is V.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib environment supplied for this task; declaration and source read with read_mathlib.

lean.type: ∀ (F V I : Type*) [Field F] [AddCommGroup V] [Module F V] [FiniteDimensional F V] [Fintype I] (z : I → V), LinearIndependent F z → Fintype.card I = Module.finrank F V → Submodule.span F (Set.range z) = ⊤
lean.proof:
intro F V I _ _ _ _ _ z hz hc
exact hz.span_eq_top_of_card_eq_finrank' hc

dependencies.justification: Direct native theorem, used to turn λ+1 independent vectors into a basis/spanning family, first over ℂ and then over K.

dependencies.statement: For any field K, abelian group M regarded as a ℤ-module, any index type I and ℤ-basis b:I→M, the scalar extension K⊗_ℤ M has a K-basis β indexed by I satisfying β(i)=1⊗b(i).

lean.type: ∀ (K M I : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℤ M] (b : Module.Basis I ℤ M), ∃ β : Module.Basis I K (TensorProduct ℤ K M), ∀ i, β i = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ (1 : K) (b i)
lean.proof:
intro K M I _ _ _ b
exact ⟨b.baseChange K, fun i => b.baseChange_apply K i⟩

dependencies.justification: Native basis scalar extension, using the canonical ℤ-algebra structure on a field. Original M⊗K is identified with K⊗M by the explicit balanced swap in B103.

dependencies.statement: For any prime p, any field K of characteristic p and any natural r<p, the image of r! in K is a unit.

origin.revision: Pinned Mathlib environment supplied for this task; declaration and source read with read_mathlib.

lean.type: ∀ (K : Type*) [Field K] (p : ℕ) [Fact (Nat.Prime p)] [CharP K p] (r : ℕ), r < p → IsUnit (Nat.factorial r : K)
lean.proof:
intro K _ p _ _ r hr
exact (IsUnit.natCast_factorial_iff_of_charP (A := K) p).2 hr

dependencies.justification: The native result is more general (rings); this closed proof specializes it to fields without changing the characteristic or strict bound. The primality typeclass is supplied from the original prime hypothesis.

dependencies.statement: For natural numbers n,k with k≤n, binom(n,k)·k!·(n−k)!=n!.

lean.type: ∀ (n k : ℕ), k ≤ n → Nat.choose n k * Nat.factorial k * Nat.factorial (n - k) = Nat.factorial n
lean.proof:
intro n k hk
exact Nat.choose_mul_factorial_mul_factorial hk

dependencies.justification: Exact natural-number factorial identity. It supplies the binomial expressions in B101 and, after casting into K, proves the binomial factors used in B103 are nonzero.

dependencies.statement: For every field F, F-vector space V, finite type I and F-basis b:I→V, finrank_F(V)=|I|.

lean.proof:
intro F V I _ _ _ _ b
exact Module.finrank_eq_card_basis b

dependencies.justification: Exact native dimension theorem; applied to the basis supplied by B003. Its finite basis also supplies finite dimensionality by spanning finitely many basis vectors.

dependencies.statement: For any field K, ℤ-modules M,N with abelian underlying groups, and ℤ-linear map f:M→N, scalar extension gives a K-linear map f_K:K⊗_ℤ M→K⊗_ℤ N satisfying f_K(c⊗m)=c⊗f(m) for every c∈K,m∈M.

lean.type: ∀ (K M N : Type*) [Field K] [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module ℤ M] [Module ℤ N] (f : M →ₗ[ℤ] N), ∃ g : TensorProduct ℤ K M →ₗ[K] TensorProduct ℤ K N, ∀ (c : K) (m : M), g (TensorProduct.tmul ℤ c m) = TensorProduct.tmul ℤ c (f m)
lean.proof:

exact ⟨f.baseChange K, fun c m => rfl⟩

dependencies.justification: Native extension of linear maps, rather than an assumed reduction homomorphism. B103 proves preservation of the needed operations from this displayed pure-tensor formula and the spanning basis of B003.

dependencies.statement: Let λ∈ℕ, V be a complex vector space of dimension λ+1, x,y,h∈End_ℂ(V) with hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y and xy−yx=h, and let 0≠v satisfy xv=0, hv=λv. Put X_r=x^r/r!, Y_r=y^r/r! and e_i=Y_i v for 0≤i≤λ. Then the e_i form a complex basis, y^{λ+1}v=0, x e_0=0, x e_i=(λ−i+1)e_{i−1} for 1≤i≤λ, y e_i=(i+1)e_{i+1} for i<λ, y e_λ=0, h e_i=(λ−2i)e_i. For every r∈ℕ, X_r e_i=binom(λ−i+r,r)e_{i−r} if r≤i and is zero otherwise; Y_r e_i=binom(i+r,r)e_{i+r} if i+r≤λ and is zero otherwise.

dependencies.justification: Concrete commutator induction, nonvanishing by repeated raising, distinct complex eigenvalues and the given dimension prove the basis. Expansion in this basis proves termination. Iteration and the factorial identity give every divided-power formula; see the full B101 argument.

dependencies.statement: Under B101's hypotheses, let M⊂V be any ℤ-submodule stable under all X_r,Y_r, and let E_ij be the complex matrix units for the e-basis. Set c_j=binom(λ,j), P=Y_λ X_λ and A_ij=X_{λ−i} P Y_{λ−j} for 0≤i,j≤λ. Then P=E_λλ and A_ij=c_j E_ij. Each A_ij restricts to a ℤ-linear endomorphism of M. For these restricted endomorphisms, A_ij A_kl= c_j A_il if j=k and is zero if j≠k. With C=∏_{t=0}^λ c_t and d_i=∏_{0≤t≤λ,t≠i} c_t, one has ∑_{i=0}^λ d_i A_ii=C·Id_M and C=c_i d_i for each i. Also (r!)X_r=x^r and (r!)Y_r=y^r on M for every r, and h restricts to M as xy−yx. No rational scalar multiplication on M is asserted.

dependencies.justification: Compute on the complex basis, then restrict equality to the injectively included lattice. Only products, sums and integer scalars occur in the identities that are restricted. The symmetry binom(λ,λ−j)=binom(λ,j) follows from B005 by cancellation of the nonzero integer factorials.

dependencies.statement: Let p be prime, K any field of characteristic p, and λ∈ℕ with λ<p. Let V,x,y,h,v satisfy B101 and M be an arbitrary admissible lattice of rank λ+1. Write U=M⊗_ℤ K, equivalently K⊗_ℤ M by the balanced swap. Then U has dimension λ+1 over K and is nonzero. Extend the lattice endomorphisms of B102 to K, denoting them by a hat. Every c_j=binom(λ,j) and C has nonzero image in K. The K-endomorphisms F_ij=(c_j mod K)^{-1}·Â_ij satisfy F_ij F_kl=δ_jk F_il and ∑_i F_ii=Id_U. For 0≤r≤λ, the induced operators satisfy X̂_r=(r! mod K)^{-1} x̂^r and Ŷ_r=(r! mod K)^{-1} ŷ^r. Consequently every K-subspace invariant under x̂ and ŷ is invariant under every F_ij; ĥ=x̂ŷ−ŷx̂ is the original induced h action.

dependencies.justification: Explicit tensor swap, native basis and map extension, and equality on a spanning pure-tensor basis transfer the integral identities. Cast B005 and apply B004 to show c_j≠0, then divide in K. This directly replaces localization, rational rank computations and the principal fractional-ideal argument.

dependencies.statement: Let F be any field, n a positive natural number, and U a finite-dimensional F-vector space of dimension n. Suppose F_ij∈End_F(U), indexed by 0≤i,j<n, satisfy F_ij F_kl=δ_jk F_il and ∑_i F_ii=Id_U. Then every F-linear subspace stable under all F_ij is either zero or U.

dependencies.justification: Given 0≠w in a nonzero stable subspace choose j with u=F_jj w≠0. The n vectors F_ij u belong to the subspace. Apply F_jk to any linear relation to obtain a_k u=0, so the vectors are independent. B002 makes them spanning. All hypotheses and the independence computation are supplied in the full proof.

dependencies.statement: For every prime p, every field K of characteristic p, every integer λ with 0≤λ<p, every complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module V(λ) of dimension λ+1 with the stated Chevalley normalizations and nonzero highest-weight vector v, and every arbitrary U_ℤ-stable admissible lattice M as defined in problem.md, the module M⊗_ℤ K is nonzero and every K-linear subspace invariant under the induced x,y,h is zero or the whole module. This includes λ=0 and p=2, and imposes no algebraic-closure hypothesis on K.

dependencies.justification: Replace the nonnegative integer λ by its natural-number representative without changing its value or range. Apply the preceding derivations to the original action and arbitrary lattice. B103 supplies dimension, nonzero space, matrix units and invariance, and B104 proves the requested dichotomy. The original complex irreducibility H is retained although dimension, the highest-weight vector and commutators suffice for this stronger argument.
